# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Goodness, this life contains only farewells and encounters, to quote Mrs. Sowerby,” Nell stated mournfully, placing her slate and books onto the table in the kitchen on June’s final day while drying her flushed eyes using a soaked handkerchief. “Thirza, wasn't it lucky that I brought an additional handkerchief to school with me today? I possessed a feeling that I would require it.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0000 }

“I didn’t expect you to care so much for Mr. Pidgeon that his departure would make you use a pair of handkerchiefs to wipe away your weeping,” Thirza remarked.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0001 }

“My tears did not fall, I believe, out of any deep affection for him,” Nell mused. “I wept simply because everyone else was weeping. Opal Pettigrew initiated it. Opal Pettigrew constantly claimed to detest Mr. Pidgeon, yet the moment he stood to deliver his parting address, she erupted into tears. Every girl subsequently broke down, one by one. Thirza, I attempted to resist. I endeavoured to recall the occasion Mr. Pidgeon forced me to sit beside Hughie—beside a male classmate; alongside the instance he omitted the ‘e’ from my name on the chalkboard; as well as his remark that I was the most ignorant pupil he had encountered in geometry and his mockery of my orthography; together with every moment he had behaved with such spite and sarcasm; yet somehow I was unable to hold out, Thirza, and I was forced to weep as well. Odette Pullen spent four weeks insisting how delighted she would be upon Mr. Pidgeon's departure and pledged that no tear would be shed by her. Nevertheless, her weeping surpassed all of ours, forcing her to obtain a handkerchief from her brother—naturally, no tears were shed by the boys—since no handkerchief had been brought by her, as she had not anticipated requiring one. Oh, Thirza, the scene was agonizing. A truly magnificent parting address was delivered by Mr. Pidgeon, commencing with, ‘The time has come for us to part.’ The effect was deeply moving. Furthermore, his own eyes contained tears, Thirza. Oh, immense sorrow and guilt consumed me over every instance I had conversed during class, sketched caricatures of him upon my slate, and ridiculed him alongside Sukey. Truly, I yearned to have been an exemplary student such as Posy Pullen. Her conscience was entirely clear. The walk home from school was accompanied by the girls' continuous weeping. At regular intervals, Carrie Mott repeated, ‘The time has come for us to part,’ which reignited our tears whenever we risked brightening up. Thirza, a profound sadness hangs over me. Yet a person cannot remain completely plunged in grief when facing a two-month holiday, can one, Thirza? On top of that, we encountered the new clergyman and his spouse travelling from the train depot. Despite my intense sorrow over the departure of Mr. Pidgeon, I was unable to suppress a slight curiosity regarding a new clergyman, was I? A great deal of beauty is possessed by his spouse. Naturally, she is not regally magnificent—it would likely be improper for a clergyman to possess a regally magnificent spouse, as an undesirable precedent might be established. It is asserted by Mrs. Sowerby that the clergyman's spouse in Stonebridge establishes a terrible precedent owing to her fashionable attire. Attired in blue muslin featuring exquisite puffed sleeves, our new clergyman's spouse wore a hat ornamented with roses. It was remarked by Odette Pullen that puffed sleeves appeared overly worldly for the spouse of a clergyman, but no such judgmental observation was uttered by me, Thirza, for the yearning for puffed sleeves is something I understand. Additionally, her tenure as a clergyman's spouse has been brief, so concessions ought to be granted, should they not? Accommodation will be provided to them by Mrs. Sowerby until the parsonage is completed.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0002 }

Should Thirza have been prompted by any reason besides her stated purpose of bringing back the quilting frames she had taken on loan the previous winter when she went to Mrs. Sowerby’s that night, it constituted a harmless flaw common to the majority of the Brierley folk. Numerous items Mrs. Sowerby had granted on loan, occasionally without any anticipation of their return, were brought back that evening by those who had borrowed them. An unfamiliar clergyman, who additionally possessed a spouse, served as a legitimate reason for inquisitiveness within a peaceful, small rural village in which exciting events occurred rarely.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0003 }

The minister whom Nell had considered deficient in imagination, old Mr. Bentley, had served as Brierley’s pastor for eighteen years. Having arrived as a widower, he continued as a widower, even though gossip systematically united him in marriage to various women during each year of his stay. Having resigned his charge in the previous February, he departed surrounded by the regrets of his congregation, the majority of whom possessed the affection arising from prolonged contact for their good old minister, notwithstanding his deficiencies as a speaker. From that time on, the Brierley church had experienced a diverse form of spiritual entertainment by hearing the numerous and different candidates and “supplies” who arrived every Sunday to deliver sermons on trial. The decision to accept or reject them rested with the fathers and mothers in Israel; nevertheless, a particular small girl with red hair who was seated meekly in the corner of the old Abernethy pew likewise possessed her own views regarding them and talked over these completely with Obed, whereas Thirza constantly refused on principle to express opinions about ministers in any way or manner.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0004 }

“It seems to me Mr. Smith was inadequate, Obed” Nell concluded at last. “According to Mrs. Sowerby, his speaking style was quite lacking, though I believe his greatest flaw mirrored Mr. Bentley’s—a complete absence of imagination. Conversely, Mr. Terry possessed far too much; his imagination overwhelmed him precisely as mine did regarding the Whispering Wood. What is more, Mrs. Sowerby claims his theological views were flawed. While Mr. Gresham was a genuinely good and pious individual, he shared an excess of humorous anecdotes that caused the congregation to laugh during services; his lack of dignity was a problem, since a minister needs to maintain a degree of dignity, doesn’t he, Obed? To my mind, Mr. Ambrose was quite appealing; however, Mrs. Sowerby investigated him specifically and discovered he lacks a wife or even a fiancée, and she asserts that stationing a young, unwed clergyman in Brierley would be disastrous, given the potential for him to wed a parishioner and cause friction. Mrs. Sowerby possesses remarkable foresight, wouldn’t you say, Obed? It pleases me greatly that Mr. Wace received the call. My preference was for him owing to his engaging sermon, combined with the fact that his praying felt genuine rather than a mere routine performance. Although Mrs. Sowerby admits he has flaws, she remarks that a faultless pastor is hardly to be anticipated for a yearly salary of seven hundred and fifty dollars, and at any rate his theological principles are firm, as she interrogated him exhaustively regarding every doctrinal detail. Furthermore, she is acquainted with his spouse's family, who are highly esteemed, with the female relatives all excelling at domestic management. Mrs. Sowerby maintains that proper doctrine from the husband coupled with effective housekeeping from the wife forms the perfect pairing for a parsonage.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0005 }

A youthful, kindly-visaged pair, the new minister and his spouse were yet enjoying their honeymoon, brimming with noble and lovely zeal for the life's labor they had selected. Brierley embraced them warmly right from the beginning. Both the aged and the youthful grew fond of the candid, sunny young man possessing lofty ideals, as well as the intelligent, mild small lady who took on the duties of manse mistress. Nell fell immediately and completely in love with Mrs. Wace. Another kindred spirit had been found by her.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0006 }

“Mrs. Wace is completely delightful,” she declared a single Sunday afternoon. “She has assumed control of our class, and she is an magnificent instructor. She stated immediately that she failed to see why it was fair that the teacher posed every question, and you are aware, Thirza, that is precisely my own long-standing opinion. She informed us that we were permitted to pose any query we desired to her, and I posed a great number. I possess a talent for posing queries, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0007 }

“I accept what you say,” Thirza declared forcefully.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0008 }

“No one else made an inquiry apart from Opal Pettigrew, who wanted to know whether a Sunday-school picnic would take place this summer. I felt that was not a particularly suitable thing to ask since it had no relation to the lesson—which concerned Daniel in the lions’ den—however, Mrs. Wace simply smiled and stated that she believed there would be one. Mrs. Wace possesses a beautiful smile; her cheeks feature such dainty dimples. I desire to have dimples in my cheeks, Thirza. Although I am far less thin than I was upon my arrival here, I still lack dimples. Had I any, maybe I could sway folks toward righteousness. Mrs. Wace mentioned that we should constantly endeavor to sway others toward righteousness. She spoke so pleasantly regarding all matters. Prior to this, I had never realized that religion could be so uplifting. I had always assumed it was somewhat gloomy, yet Mrs. Wace’s version is not, and I would wish to become a Christian if I might resemble her. I would have no desire to resemble Mr. Superintendent Bell.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0009 }

“To talk like that regarding Mr. Bell is quite wicked of you,” Thirza remarked sternly. “A truly virtuous man is what Mr. Bell is.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0010 }

“Oh, naturally he is good,” Nell concurred, “yet he does not appear to derive any solace from it. Were I able to be good, I would sing and dance the entire day on account of being happy about it. Mrs. Wace is likely too advanced in years to sing and dance, and it certainly would lack dignity for a minister’s spouse. Nevertheless, I can simply sense her joy in being a Christian, and that she would remain one even were it possible for her to reach heaven without doing so.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0011 }

“I guess we ought to invite Mr. and Mrs. Wace over for tea one of these days,” Thirza remarked thoughtfully. “They have visited practically every place except this one. Let me think. Upcoming Wednesday should be a suitable date to entertain them. However, do not mention a thing to Obed regarding it, because if he were aware of their arrival he would invent a reason to be absent then. He had grown so accustomed to Mr. Bentley that he was comfortable with him, yet he will struggle to adjust to a different pastor, and a different pastor’s spouse will terrify him completely.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0012 }

“I will keep it as quiet as the grave,” promised Nell. “However, Thirza, is it all right if I bake a cake for the event? I would be thrilled to contribute something for Mrs. Wace, and you are aware that I have become quite skilled at baking a cake now.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0013 }

“It is possible for you to bake a layer cake,” Thirza pledged.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0014 }

Extensive arrangements were made at Grey Shutters throughout Monday and Tuesday. Serving tea to the minister and his spouse was a grave and significant event, and Thirza was resolved to outshine all the housekeepers in Brierley. Nell was filled with wild delight and excitement. Sitting on the large red rocks beside the Nymph’s Well during Tuesday evening's dusk, she discussed everything with Isolde while they created rainbows upon the water using small twigs coated in fir balsam.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0015 }

“Isolde, every single thing is prepared, with the exception of my cake that I am supposed to bake in the morning, alongside the baking-powder biscuits that Thirza is going to prepare right before the time for tea. Isolde, I promise you that these two days have been extremely busy for Thirza and me. Hosting a minister’s family for tea involves a great deal of responsibility. An event like this has never happened to me until now. Our pantry is something you really ought to look at. It is a remarkable vision. Jellied chicken and cold tongue are going to be served by us. We will serve a pair of jelly varieties, one red and one yellow, as well as whipped cream, lemon pie, cherry pie, three varieties of cookies, fruit cake, Thirza’s well-known yellow plum preserves which she reserves specifically for ministers, pound cake, layer cake, plus the previously mentioned biscuits; furthermore, both new and old bread will be provided, should the minister suffer from dyspepsia and be unable to consume new bread. Mrs. Sowerby claims that ministers suffer from dyspepsia, but my opinion is that Mr. Wace has not served as a minister for a sufficient duration to suffer ill effects from it. Thinking about my layer cake makes me freeze up completely. Oh, Isolde, suppose it turns out badly! Last night brought a dream where a horrifying goblin featuring a large layer cake as a head pursued me everywhere.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0016 }

“It’s going to be good, no doubt,” affirmed Isolde, who was a exceptionally comforting kind of companion. “I’m certain that portion of the one you prepared which we ate for lunch at Larkrise a fortnight back was absolutely splendid.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0017 }

“Yes; but cakes possess such an awful tendency to end up ruined precisely at the moment you most desire them to prove successful,” sighed Nell, launching a twig that was exceptionally heavily coated in balsam. “Nonetheless, I imagine my only option is to rely on Providence while ensuring I remember the flour. Oh, see, Isolde, what a beautiful rainbow! Do you think the dryad might emerge once we depart and use it as a scarf?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0018 }

“You are aware that dryads do not exist,” Isolde stated. Because her mother had discovered the Whispering Wood and shown clear anger about it, Isolde had ceased all subsequent imaginative mimicry and considered it unwise to foster a mindset that believed even in inoffensive dryads.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0019 }

“However, picturing it there is extremely simple,” Nell stated. “Prior to retiring each evening, I gaze through my window, asking myself whether the dryad actually sits in this spot, utilizing the spring as a mirror to comb her hair. On occasion, I search the morning dew for her tracks. Oh, Isolde, do not lose your belief in the dryad!”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0020 }

Wednesday morning arrived. Nell arose at dawn since her great excitement prevented her from sleeping. Because she had dabbled in the spring during the previous evening, she had contracted a bad head cold; however, only total pneumonia could have dampened her enthusiasm for cooking that morning. Following breakfast, she set about preparing her cake. Upon finally closing the oven door on it, she took a deep breath.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0021 }

“Thirza, I’m certain nothing was left out on this occasion. Do you believe it will swell up, though? What if the baking powder might be bad? The new can provided what I used. According to Mrs. Sowerby, a person can never rely on securing quality baking powder these days since all products are so impure. It is Mrs. Sowerby's opinion that the Government should address the issue, yet she claims a Tory Government will never act on it in our lifetime. Thirza, suppose that cake fails to rise?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0022 }

“We’ll have plenty without it” expressed Thirza’s emotionless attitude regarding the matter.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0023 }

The cake actually rose, nevertheless, emerging from the oven with the featherlight lightness of golden foam. Radiant with joy, Nell pressed its layers together using ruby jelly and, within her mind, envisioned Mrs. Wace consuming a portion and perhaps requesting a second helping!
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0024 }

“Thirza, you will certainly utilize the finest set of tea, will you not?” she inquired. “Am I able to adorn the table using wild roses alongside ferns?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0025 }

“That is complete rubbish to my mind,” Thirza scoffed. “As I see it, the food itself is important, whereas fancy trimmings are not.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0026 }

“Mrs. Pembroke’s table was decorated,” remarked Nell, who was not completely free of serpent-like shrewdness, “and she received a graceful compliment from the minister. It was a banquet for both the eye and the palate, according to him.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0027 }

“Very well, act according to your wishes,” stated Thirza, who was fully resolved to avoid being outdone by Mrs. Pembroke or anyone else. “Just ensure that you preserve sufficient space for the plates and the victuals.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0028 }

Nell exerted every effort to deck the setting using a style and method intended to outdo Mrs. Pembroke's completely. Possessing a wealth of ferns and roses alongside a naturally refined artistic sensibility, she rendered the tea table so visually stunning that the minister and his wife, upon being seated before it, uttered joint exclamations regarding its exquisite charm.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0029 }

“Nell is responsible for this,” Thirza remarked with stern impartiality; and Nell considered the pleased expression on Mrs. Wace’s face to be an amount of joy nearly exceeding what this life could offer.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0030 }

Obed had been included, though solely goodness and Nell understood how he had been enticed into joining the group. His extreme shyness and agitation had caused Thirza to abandon all hope for him, yet Nell managed him so capably that he was currently seated at the board wearing his finest attire and a white collar, conversing with the minister in a manner that was far from dull. Not a single word was uttered by him to Mrs. Wace, though that was likely too much to anticipate.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0031 }

Everything proceeded as joyfully as a wedding until the passing of Nell’s layer cake. Having been served a confusing number of dishes earlier, Mrs. Wace turned it down. However, Thirza, noticing how disappointed Nell looked, spoke with a smile:
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0032 }

“Oh, Mrs. Wace, you really have to have a slice of this. Nell baked it specifically for you.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0033 }

“If so, I have to try some,” Mrs. Wace laughed, taking a fat triangle for herself, which the minister and Thirza did as well.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0034 }

A bite was taken of hers by Mrs. Wace, and an extremely strange look passed over her features; she uttered not a single word, though, but persisted in consuming it. Seeing that look, Thirza hurried to sample the cake.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0035 }

“Nell Harcourt!” she cried out, “whatever did you add to that cake?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0036 }

“Only the ingredients specified in the recipe, Thirza,” Nell exclaimed, her face showing deep distress. “Oh, is something wrong?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0037 }

“Very well! That is just dreadful. Mr. Wace, do not attempt to consume it. Nell, sample it for yourself. Which flavor did you add?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0038 }

“Vanilla,” Nell remarked, her cheeks flushed bright red with embarrassment once she had sampled the cake. “Just vanilla. Oh, Thirza, the baking powder has to be to blame. I was already doubtful about that bak—”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0039 }

“Baking powder my foot! Fetch the vanilla bottle that you worked with and hand it to me.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0040 }

Nell hurried off to the pantry and came back carrying a little bottle, somewhat full of a brown fluid, which bore a yellowed label reading, “Best Vanilla.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0041 }

Thirza accepted it, removed the cork, and took a whiff of it.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0042 }

“Heaven help us, Nell, you used Anodyne Liniment to season that cake. After smashing the liniment container a week ago, I transferred the remaining portion into a used, vacant vanilla jar. My own failure to caution you means I am somewhat to blame, I guess—yet in the name of mercy, was it impossible for you to have caught its scent?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0043 }

Under this twofold shame, Nell broke down crying.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0044 }

“I couldn’t—my cold was so severe!” and uttering these words, she precipitously escaped to the gable chamber, where she threw herself onto the bed and cried like someone who declines all solace.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0045 }

Before long a faint footfall rang upon the steps and someone walked into the chamber.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0046 }

“Oh, Thirza,” wept Nell, not raising her eyes, “I am ruined eternally. I can never overcome this shame. People will find out—word always spreads in Brierley. Isolde is going to inquire about my cake, forcing me to confess what happened. Everybody will forever single me out as the person who put anodyne liniment in a cake to flavor it. Hughie—the male students at school will continue to mock it indefinitely. Oh, Thirza, provided you possess any fraction of Christian compassion, do not force me to clean the dishes downstairs following this event. I am willing to scrub them once the minister and his wife leave, but meeting Mrs. Wace's gaze ever again is impossible for me. She might believe I attempted to poison her. Mrs. Sowerby claims to be acquainted with an orphan girl who attempted to poison the person who took care of her. However, the liniment contains no poison. It is intended for internal consumption—even if not inside cakes. Will you please inform Mrs. Wace of that, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0047 }

“Why don't you leap to your feet and inform her of that directly,” suggested a cheerful voice.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0048 }

Nell leaped out of bed, only to see Mrs. Wace beside her, watching her with amused eyes.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0049 }

“My dear little girl, you mustn’t weep this way,” she remarked, truly unsettled by the tragic expression on Nell’s face. “Why, it’s merely a comical error that any person could commit.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0050 }

“Oh, no, only I could commit a blunder like that,” Nell uttered in a dejected manner. “And my intention was to bake that cake so wonderfully for your sake, Mrs. Wace.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0051 }

“Indeed, I am aware, my dear. I give you my word that your generosity and consideration mean just as much to me as though everything had gone well. You must stop weeping now, and instead accompany me downstairs so you can display your flower garden to me. According to Miss Abernethy, you possess a small patch that belongs entirely to you. I wish to view it, because flowers hold a great deal of interest for me.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0052 }

Nell allowed herself to be taken downstairs and consoled, thinking how truly fortunate it was that Mrs. Wace shared her disposition. No further mention was made of the liniment cake, and as the visitors departed, Nell realized that she had derived greater pleasure from the night than might have been anticipated, given that awful event. Still, a heavy sigh escaped her.
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0053 }

“Is it not lovely to consider, Thirza, that a fresh day arrives tomorrow, completely free of errors so far?”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0054 }

“I am certain you will commit many therein,” Thirza remarked. “I have never met anyone who equals your knack for error, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0055 }

“Indeed, and I am fully aware of it,” Nell conceded sorrowfully. “However, Thirza, have you ever observed a single hopeful aspect regarding me? I do not repeat a blunder.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0056 }

“I fail to see how that offers much advantage when you are constantly creating additional ones.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0057 }

“Oh, is it not clear to you, Thirza? A person can only commit so many errors, and once I have made every single one, I will finally be done with them. I find great comfort in that idea.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0058 }

“Indeed, you ought to head off and feed those pigs the cake,” Thirza remarked. “No person could possibly consume it, not even Tobias Boute.”
{: #nw-v01-c21-p0059 }
